locator.section: 9.1 Hydrocarbons (retro-Diels-Alder of the cyclohexene molecular ion)

evidence.curator_note: First (ring-opening) alpha cleavage of the stepwise retro-Diels-Alder of cyclohexene. Book draws 0 arc(s) for this step inside eq 9.11: eq 9.11 branches off the same neutral cyclohexene structure through a bare arrow labelled only 'alpha', so the arrows for the ionization and this first cleavage are not repeated here. The identical ring-opening alpha cleavage IS drawn with 2 arcs one line above on the same page, on the cyclohexene molecular ion of eq 9.10; moves <1,2> correspond to those two printed arcs (dot on map 2 into the forming map2=map3 pi bond; one electron of the map3-map4 sigma bond into that same pi bond) and move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). LOCALIZATION (convention B): molecular ion written localized as C1(+)-C2(.) exactly as printed. The '-e-' ionization of neutral cyclohexene drawn on the page is not encoded as a step (electron count is not conserved by ionization); the record starts at [M]+. m/z 82.

Second alpha cleavage, which completes the retro-Diels-Alder: the primary radical (map 4) drives homolysis of the map5-map6 bond, expelling neutral ethylene (drawn on the page as the bare vertical double line) and retaining the charge on the C4H6 fragment, m/z 54. Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page - the book prints the dot on the C4H6 product instead). Drawn arc 1 = the fishhook from the printed dot (map 4) into the map4-map5 bond; drawn arc 2 = the fishhook from the map5-map6 bond into that same forming pi bond. LOCALIZATION / RESONANCE (convention C): the intermediate is printed here fully localized - '+' beside the lower-right vertex (map 1) and the double bond drawn on the upper-right diagonal (map2=map3) - and this record uses exactly that form; the m/z 54 product is likewise printed as the DISTONIC form .CH2-CH(+)-CH=CH2 (dot on map 6, '+' on map 1), not as the closed butadiene radical cation CH2=CH-CH=CH2(+.), and this record encodes the drawn distonic form (same species by resonance, C4H6+., m/z 54). NO PRINTED INTENSITY: 'm/z 54' is labelled but no percentage appears anywhere in eq 9.11, so relative_intensity is omitted (the 80% figure for cyclohexene's m/z 54 quoted in chapter 4 is not on this page).

rule_index.json has NO chapter-9 entries (by_equation covers only 4.x and 8.x), so there is no rule indexed under '9.11'. Cross-linked instead to the rules that VERIFIABLY encode the same two bond changes. (1) wikipedia.py dielsAdler_1 '[C]1[C+]2[C.]3[C]4[C]5[C]6{-}1>>[C.]5[C]6[C]1[C+]2[C]3{=}[C]4' = step_alpha1_ring_opening: with rule atoms (2,3,4,5,6,1) -> record maps (1,2,3,4,5,6) it cleaves the ring bond map3-map4, forms the map2=map3 pi bond and relocates the radical from map2 to map4; the cleaved bond IS incident to map3, the atom that forms the new pi bond, so the geometry is correct. RDKit-VERIFIED: the reactant pattern matches this record's cyclohexene molecular ion (1 hit, maps 1-2-3-4-5-6). (2) wikipedia.py dielsAdler_2a '[C.]1[C]2[C]3[C+]4[C]5{=}[C]6>>[C]1{=}[C]2.[C.]3[C+]4[C]5{=}[C]6' = step_alpha2_ethylene_loss: rule atoms (1..6) -> record maps (4,5,6,1,2,3); it cleaves map5-map6, forms the map4=map5 pi bond of the departing NEUTRAL ethylene and keeps the charge on the .CH2-CH(+)-CH=CH2 fragment - exactly the drawn m/z 54 product. RDKit-VERIFIED: matches the ring-opened intermediate (1 hit, maps 4-5-6-1-2-3). Both rules live in wikipedia.py and are therefore NOT in rule_index.json (the index only scans IMS_chap4_examples.py, IMS_chap8_examples.py and IMS_bookCover.py). MISMATCHES FOUND among the indexed candidates: IMS_4_31_alpha1 and IMS_4_31_alpha2 (indexed under eq 4.31, the German-edition retro-Diels-Alder) describe the same two steps but both require a CARBON substituent (rule map 1) on the ring atom that becomes the radical, so they do NOT match plain cyclohexene - RDKit-VERIFIED: 0 hits on this record's molecular ion / intermediate, 1 hit on 4-phenylcyclohexene. IMS_4_30 '[C.]1[C]2[C]3[C+]4[C]5{=}[C]6>>[C.]1[C+]2.[C]3{=}[C]4[C]5{=}[C]6' (and its twin wikipedia.py dielsAdler_2b) DOES match the intermediate but is the CHARGE-MIGRATION channel: it puts the charge on the two-carbon fragment (ionized ethylene, m/z 28) and expels neutral butadiene, i.e. the opposite charge partition to the m/z 54 product drawn in eq 9.11, so it does not support this record.
